beats.text: Want an assistant of your own? It can be {pictures}just pictures and JSON, or {code}a .NET project with the SDK.
Let's see {nocode}one without code, {code}one with code, how to {try}try it, and how to {share}share it.
Without code, it's a folder: {manifest}assistant.json, {character}character.json, {icon}an icon, and {frames}its pictures, PNG with transparency.
Each {anims}animation has a name: {idle}idle, the only one you need, {walk}walk, {talk}talk, {listen}listen, {think}think. A missing one {fallback}uses another.

K-Desktop moves it: it {stands}stands on the taskbar or on your windows, {strolls}strolls, and {sleeps}sleeps when you're away. And it {talks}talks, thinks and uses tools like any other. {pip}Pip is a complete example.
{pack}pack.ps1 zips the folder into a .kai, and you {open}open it with K-Desktop to install it.
With code, {install}install the template from NuGet, and {new}dotnet new kdassistant makes the project. {build}Every build leaves the .kai ready.
Your class {iassistant}implements IAssistant: it {draws}draws itself, has {hit}a click area, and {tick}Tick says how long it can sleep.

K-Desktop asks for {gestures}gestures: what it wants, never how. {press}Press a button, {move}move a window, {point}point at something. Knowing just {min}Communicate and React is enough: for the rest, the module does the action itself.
To try it without installing, run {dev}KDesktop.exe --assistant-dev with your project folder. It {reload}reloads it on every build.
{settings}settings.json gives it tabs in its settings, and {panel}panel.json its own panel. K-Desktop draws them, {nocode}without loading your code.
{keygen}kaisign keygen makes your key, once. From then on, {signed}every build signs the .kai, and K-Desktop {check}checks that nobody changed it.
Then put it in {catalog}a catalog: a JSON at a fixed address that says where each package is. With {updates}updates in its manifest, K-Desktop offers its new versions.
One last tip: {docs}the documentation has it all: {host}what the host gives you, {gestures}the gestures, and {api}the API reference.
That's the whole series. {next}Now, make it yours.
